flashcard_questions.q: Which British prime minister was one of the Big Three?
Which French leader was nicknamed “The Tiger”?
How many nations attended the Paris Peace Conference?
In which month and year did the Paris Peace Conference begin?
Which country was not invited to the peace negotiations?
How many British soldiers had died by the 1918 election?
Why did Lloyd George privately want to keep Germany strong?
flashcard_questions.a: Crippling Germany would damage British trade.

flashcard_questions.q: How old was Clemenceau when the peace conference began?
How many French soldiers were killed in the war?
How many casualties did the USA suffer in the war?
Wilson published his Fourteen Points in ____.
What was the fourteenth of Wilson’s Fourteen Points?
flashcard_questions.a: A League of Nations to settle disputes between countries.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Wilson mean by self-determination?
flashcard_questions.a: The right of a people to choose its own government.

flashcard_questions.q: Why did Britain and France resist self-determination?
Which body refused to ratify the treaty, keeping America out of the League?

notes: 15 cards: 4 person-to-significance, 5 figure, 3 event/date (1 cloze on January 1918), 3 cause-effect. Avoided listing the Big Three or the Fourteen Points in one answer; each leader gets his own front.
